title: One economy, five steps

cases.label: Baseline
cases.status_label: All numerical checks passed · 10,000 markets · two periods

steps.title: Firms differ
steps.explanation: Productivity changes; firm identities stay the same.
steps.alt: Firms differ from the solved economy
steps.caption: Market 1, fixed in advance. Teal: period 1; coral: period 2. Each firm’s productivity changes, but the economy is stationary: across all firms, its distribution is the same in both periods.

steps.title: Shares settle
steps.explanation: Prices and demand shares adjust until they agree.
steps.alt: Shares settle from the solved economy
steps.caption: Actual updates for the largest final-share firm in market 1, first exit round.

steps.title: Labor clears
steps.explanation: Every worker produces goods or covers fixed operations.
steps.alt: Labor clears from the solved economy
steps.caption: Each bar = 100 employed workers. The dark marker is household labor supplied. The two periods look alike because the economy is stationary; which firms operate still changes (see 02.1).

steps.title: Firms leave
steps.explanation: After exits, solve prices and employment again.
steps.alt: Firms leave from the solved economy
steps.caption: Teal: period 1; coral: period 2. Rounds are solver steps, not years. Both periods end with almost the same number of firms because the economy is stationary.

steps.title: Compare the fit
steps.explanation: Teal = model. Coral marker = year-2000 data.
steps.alt: Compare the fit from the solved economy
steps.caption: Each row has its own scale. pp = percentage points; markup is a ratio.
